analysis:
This batch contains documentation only: changelog.d/glm-variable-frame-rate-video.md (new, lines 1-4) and docs/architecture/inference.md (head 810-813, 829, 1896-1899). They describe two behavior changes whose Swift implementation is not in this batch.

1. The GLM5Next processor now indexes variable-frame-rate MP4/QuickTime tracks in presentation order instead of refusing them. Frame i is timed at i/nominalFrameRate, followed by the unchanged 2 FPS sampler.
2. MediaIngest.admittedVideoDataURIHeaders now also admits the data:video/mov and data:video/x-m4v labels on the shared GLM/Gemma/Qwen path. The container is still sniffed from the bytes by MemoryBackedVideoAsset.

The docs state that existing bounds are unchanged: maximumDecodedBytes 512 MiB, maxVideoDurationSeconds 600, maxMediaDecodedBytes 25 MiB and the 28,532 visual-token cap. They also state that media stays excluded from prefix lookup and capture (CBv2Request.permitsHybridCheckpoint), so T-041 cache isolation is not affected. The Nemotron Super labels are unchanged.

Threats touched: TB-007/A-001 (decrypted inline video handled in-process) and T-050 (video plaintext temp files). The new labels do not imply disk writes, but the docs do not confirm this.

Questions for integration, which need the Swift source:
- nominalFrameRate for a VFR or malformed track can be 0, NaN, very small or very large. Timing i/rate could then produce division by zero, infinite timestamps, or a sample plan that selects a huge frame range. Check that the sampler stays bounded by the duration cap and the decoded-byte cap.
- Check that every frame up to the last sampled one is still bounded by the frame-count and decode-time limits.
- Check that the added labels cannot bypass the byte sniffing.
- Check that MemoryBackedVideoAsset keeps video in memory, with no temp file (T-050).

No regression is evidenced by the documentation alone.
